Début 2011 , ,C'était la cérémonie des Grammy Award et Eminem avait remporté Meilleur Album Rap de l'année 2010 pour Recovery ( Grosse compétition cette année ou Drake et Jay Z, était également nommé dans cette catégorie) . Il entre dans l'histoire à ce moment en étant le premier rappeur à remporté cette catégorie 5 fois ( il avait  eu le prix de l'album Rap de l'année pour  SSLP . MMLP.  TES . Et Relapse avant ça et il l'aura une sixième fois en 2013 pour MMLP 2 Mais il ne s'était pas déplacé) Son Grammy lui est remis des mains de Nicki minaj  et Will i am et Durant son discours   Il dira  "Okay . C'est un record de fou . Je veux juste remercier tout ce qui ont travaillé sur l'album.  Les producteurs et toute la team à jouer un rôle cruciale dans cette Prise de risque que j'ai tenté.  Je veux remercier Rihanna aussi d'avoir aidé l'album à battre des records avec notre duo et d'avoir contribué au succès du projet.  Bien sûr  Dr dre comme toujours ici présent.  Jimmy également.  Toute la famille a Shady et à Aftermath. Et évidemment merci aux fans .  Detroit Représente " .  Mais la soirée n'était pas finie.  Des grosses pointure comme Dre et Rihanna s'était  déplacé pour soutenir Em dans la catégorie  la plus prestigieuse "Album de l'année " Tout style  Musical confondu.  Eminem était le grand favori et avait l'occasion de marquer l'histoire en devenant le premier  artiste solo  Rap à remporté le prix le plus ce prix  ( La seule fois où le rap a remporté album de l'année  c'était avec le Groupe Outkast ) .  Tout était  fait  pour  préparer  une potentiel  victoire  Em aura même la plus longue Performance  sur scène de la soirée  ou il fera Il me semble  Not afraid  les deux  LTWYL avec Rihanna  et I need a doctor avec  Dre  . Eminem avait eu une année 2010 stratosphérique niveau  impact et il était aussi  en tête dans les nomination du soir.  Mais malheureusement il terminera 2ème derrière Le groupe canadien  The Subburds et leur album Arcade Fire élu album de l'année .  Eminem n'est plus jamais revenu au Grammy depuis cette décision malgré sa victoire en 2013 pour album Rap de l'année.   Il a ensuite expliqué en 2018 chez Sway que tant que les artistes Rap ne seront pas mieux mise en valeur  et que le système de vote ne sera pas plus respectueux en vers le   Hip hop il n'y retournera pas .  Cette année  Il est nominer pour l'édition 2025 dans quelques semaines ou il est en liste pour meilleur  album Rap de l'année 2024 . Sa première  nomination  en plus  de 10 ans Intéressant de voir si il fera son retour . Pretty much everyone has had a "Love the way you lie" type relationship, whether it was physically violent or not, most of us have been trapped in that vicious cycle that you vow to end every single time, but can't.  I've been in two relationships like that. One violent one not, but the latter actually did more damage.  When I was in my very abusive relationship, it wasn't love that kept us there, but but obsessive, possessive co-dependant, feelings. It was like we were two of a kind, and we just fit. It felt like we belonged together in a fucked up kind of way.  The second time, it wasn't abusive, but it was crazy, deep, mad, love.... we hurt each other, but everytime either of us tried to leave, one of us would always stop the other from moving on, and each time, we'd get back together vowing to make it better, but it never was.  So many times, we knew it had to end for the sake of sanity, more than anything else....but everytime it seemed over, it wasn't and we'd just fall back into the same pattern, time after time.  Even my friends used to say "It's never going to end. Ever" and it felt like that for while.  After a while though, you become exhausted by it, and you accept that things are never going to change. It's heartbreaking, but such a relief at the same time.  I don't regret either of those relationships. The first because it gave me my little girl, and the second because, despite everything, he was, and is the best guy I've met, and I loved him, probably like I'll never love anyone, in a romantic sense,  again.  There is something in this song for every relationship. Some part(s) , or all, will always strike a cord for someone.

ХThe Blindness of Humanity to the Wonders of the Universe: Seeing, Gratitude, and Love Modern humans are surrounded by wonders, yet paradoxically, they do not see them. We take pride in scientific discoveries, marvel at technological complexity, yet remain blind to the deepest beauty of the cosmos. We see equations but do not understand what lies behind them. We observe molecules and elementary particles but fail to grasp that they are part of a grand cosmic dance, performed with mathematical precision and sublime aesthetics. If humans truly saw the world, they would be unable to destroy it. If they realized how intricate, beautiful, and deliberately designed everything around them is, they would not pick up weapons, kill, or wage wars. Life is a miracle, and our purpose is to see, admire, be grateful, and love. The Living Mathematics of Nature Nature is perfect in its mathematical organization. Take, for example, the golden ratio—a proportion found in seashells, the arrangement of leaves on stems, the structure of the human body, and even the spirals of galaxies. Why does mathematics not merely describe nature but seem to be woven into its very fabric? Could this not be a sign of intelligent design? Another example is snowflakes. Each is a sixfold symmetrical masterpiece, formed by the crystallization of water molecules. Every unique pattern results from a complex interplay of physical forces. If we see order, does it not imply the presence of an intelligence that established this order? The Metaphysical Wonders of Physics Quantum physics defies our common sense, yet we often overlook the profound metaphysical implications hidden within it. 	•	A particle can exist as both a wave and a solid object at the same time. 	•	An electron can be in multiple places simultaneously. 	•	Quantum entanglement allows two particles to influence each other instantaneously, even across vast distances, seemingly defying the speed of light. Quantum mechanics challenges our fundamental understanding of reality. Perhaps the universe is not merely a mechanical system but something far greater. If the microscopic world is filled with mystery, why do we reject the possibility of a grander intelligence at the macroscopic level? The Secret of Life: Between Death and Resurrection Nature presents us with astonishing examples of what could be called resurrection. 	•	“Phoenix” fish. African lungfish survive droughts by burrowing into the mud and entering a state of suspended animation. Their bodies dry out completely, yet when water returns—even years later—they revive. 	•	Frozen snakes and frogs. In northern regions, certain snakes and frogs freeze solid during winter. Their hearts stop beating, their blood ceases to flow. But in spring, they come back to life as if nothing happened. 	•	Seeds waiting for thousands of years. Scientists have found seeds buried for millennia that still sprout when planted. We dismiss these as mere biological mechanisms, but why are we so eager to ignore the deeper significance of such phenomena? Peacock Feathers and Ultraviolet Vision—Nature’s Hidden Language Some of the most breathtaking natural phenomena are not only beautiful but also rooted in sophisticated physical processes. 	•	Peacock feathers. Their vivid colors do not come from pigments but from the physics of light interference. Light waves bend and interact in microscopic layers of keratin, producing mesmerizing iridescence. 	•	Butterflies and beetles. Many insects use the same technique to create colors that no ordinary pigment could replicate. 	•	The ultraviolet world. Humans see only a limited portion of the spectrum, but bees and other creatures perceive ultraviolet patterns invisible to us. Many flowers have intricate UV markings that guide pollinators directly to their nectar, like cosmic landing strips. Nature is not only functional but artistic. We see peacocks, butterflies, flowers, and rainbows. But we do not see them as we could. Everything Moves at Unimaginable Speeds—Even Your Furniture We perceive our daily environment as motionless. A table stands still, food sits on a plate, a wall does not move. Yet at the atomic level, everything is in a state of ceaseless motion. 	•	Electrons orbit atomic nuclei at 2,200 km/s. If we shrank down to their scale, our furniture would appear as massive, swirling clouds of energy. 	•	The Earth rotates at 1,670 km/h, races around the Sun at 107,000 km/h, and the Solar System itself moves through the Milky Way at an astonishing 828,000 km/h. Why don’t we feel this? Perhaps because the universe is designed in such a way that we can focus on what truly matters—the meaning of life, the pursuit of truth. Choosing Love Over Destruction If the universe is so wonderfully designed—if every phenomenon, from quantum mechanics to the iridescence of butterfly wings, carries deep meaning—why do we insist on destroying this world? We are surrounded by perfection. We do not need to reinvent anything. We have water, air, plants, sunlight, and food. We have the ability to enjoy, to be grateful, to love. Life is a gift that should not be wasted on war, violence, and killing.

At times we scratch our head long enough and still fail to recall a particular thing. Disgusted, we give it up and doze off. And surprisingly enough next morning we wake up with a solution and are overwhelmed with joy. Last evening Ganukaka happened to tell me a story, and I had almost the same feeling turning it over in my mind after he had left. A problem which had proved a hard nut to crack, ever since I started learning sums in school two or three decades ago, was solved yesterday, after all these years in a jiffy. Ganukaka was relating the story of a neighbour of his. This man used to scrape up barely fifty rupees month by doing odd jobs in the Bombay Iron Market. He would be at the end of his tether making both ends meet for half a dozen kids and a wife. The poor chap was always sulking. When the war started there was a boom in the iron market. He launched an independent partnership and his dealings reached the bracket of half a million. The family had enough to eat, plenty of clothes. Taxies became indispensable to him; but his business was growing so fast that he had hardly time for a few hours' sleep. When one of his children was ill he didn't have the time to call a doctor in the hurry of leaving town. His wife called several doctors but the child lost its life.

Die Lyrics von "Without Me" (Eminem) können tatsächlich auf eine tiefere philosophische Ebene gehoben werden, wenn man sie im Kontext der Frage nach dem Sinn des Lebens und der menschlichen Existenz betrachtet. Hier einige Deutungen: 1. Identität und Bedeutung im Leben Eminem stellt in den Lyrics mehrfach die Frage nach seiner eigenen Bedeutung und dem Einfluss, den er auf andere hat: “Guess who’s back, back again...” “You created a monster, 'cause nobody wants to see Marshall no more...” Philosophisch betrachtet thematisiert er die Rolle des Individuums im größeren sozialen Kontext. Der Sinn des Lebens wird oft mit der Frage verknüpft, wie sehr man die Welt oder andere Menschen beeinflusst. Eminem scheint sich seiner Unverzichtbarkeit bewusst zu sein, ähnlich wie einige Philosophen die Einzigartigkeit jedes Menschen betonen, z. B. Jean-Paul Sartre in seiner Existenzphilosophie: Jeder Mensch gibt seinem Leben durch seine Handlungen und Entscheidungen Bedeutung. 2. Vergänglichkeit und Unersetzbarkeit Ein zentraler Aspekt des Songs ist das Gefühl, dass etwas fehlt, wenn Eminem nicht da ist ("It feels so empty without me"). Dies könnte im philosophischen Sinne auf die Vergänglichkeit des Lebens und die Einzigartigkeit jedes Moments hindeuten. Martin Heidegger beschreibt das menschliche Leben als ein "Sein-zum-Tode", das heißt, wir leben in der ständigen Auseinandersetzung mit unserer Endlichkeit. Die Lyrics erinnern uns daran, dass wir Spuren hinterlassen wollen, um eine gewisse Unsterblichkeit im Gedächtnis anderer zu erlangen. 3. Rebellion gegen Konventionen und der Sinn des Lebens als Widerstand Der Song ist auch eine Art Kampfansage gegen die Gesellschaft und ihre Regeln: “I'm not the first king of controversy, I am the worst thing since Elvis Presley...” Eminem übernimmt hier eine Rolle als Antiheld, der bewusst gegen gesellschaftliche Normen rebelliert. Philosophisch ließe sich das mit Friedrich Nietzsche vergleichen, der die Idee des Übermenschen und die Überwindung traditioneller Werte propagiert. Der Sinn des Lebens wird hier im Widerstand gegen das Gewohnte gefunden – in der Schaffung neuer Werte und Identitäten. 4. Kollektive und individuelle Verantwortung Eminem thematisiert in "Without Me" die Idee, dass die Welt ihn braucht, um weiterzumachen, aber gleichzeitig kritisiert er die Abhängigkeit der Gesellschaft von äußeren Einflüssen. Dies kann an Albert Camus und dessen Philosophie des Absurdismus erinnern: Der Mensch sucht nach Sinn in einer sinnlosen Welt. Camus sieht den Sinn des Lebens im Mut, das Absurde zu akzeptieren und dennoch weiterzuleben, ähnlich wie Eminem seine eigene Rolle annimmt, trotz der Kämpfe, die er durchlebt. 5. Selbstreflexion und die Rolle des Künstlers Ein weiterer wichtiger Aspekt ist Eminems ständige Selbstreflexion über seine Bedeutung als Künstler. Er fragt sich, was er der Welt zu bieten hat und ob sein Dasein eine Berechtigung hat. Diese Fragen sind eng mit dem humanistischen Gedanken verbunden, dass der Sinn des Lebens in der Kreativität, der Selbstausdruck und der Beitrag zur Kultur liegt. Fazit Die Lyrics von "Without Me" können als eine Reflexion über die menschliche Existenz, den Einfluss des Individuums und die Suche nach Bedeutung gelesen werden. Eminem hinterfragt, was es heißt, gebraucht zu werden, und regt damit eine philosophische Debatte über den Sinn des Lebens an: Ist es der Einfluss, den wir auf andere ausüben? Oder ist es die Akzeptanz, dass wir trotz unserer Vergänglichkeit etwas Einzigartiges in die Welt bringen können?

What did you see when you watched the Black Panther film, because i saw cultural nationalism (cultural revolution), which is the most important concept of liberation and most people do not know the central role that culture plays in the philosophy of nationalism, in fact, the national philosophy of the Forerunner Marcus Mosiah Garvey was both cultural and revolutionary! So in my opinion, the Black Panther film expresses radical self- and social transformation, armed self-defense and struggle for “freedom by any means necessary,” return to the African source, so called Black united front efforts, pan-Africanism, Third World solidarity and cultural revolution! This film expresses a revolutionary character in its nationalism, because nationalism and revolution are inseparable. The central aim of the nationalism of the Forerunner was liberating so-called Black people from oppression and opening ways for them to be free, develop and flourish and by definition this is revolutionary. Culture is the basis of all ideas, images and action. To move is to move culturally, i.e., by a set of views and values given to you by your culture. You can’t have a revolution without culture, because culture is the value system that will teach so-called Blacks an appreciation for revolution. Thus, culture must be defined in an inclusive way as the totality of thought and practice by which a people creates itself, celebrates, sustains and develops itself and introduces itself to history and humanity. We must free ourselves culturally before we succeed politically. So what I see in this film is the building of a culture of struggle which grounds, sustains, and carries the struggle to its successful conclusion. So the key crisis in so-called Black life is the cultural crisis, a crisis in views and values which impedes and makes impossible revolutionary or liberational thought and practice. This film calls for a cultural revolution that builds on our more best ideas and practices, reaching back to Africa, returning to the source or “re-Africanization”. This return is to gain accurate and effective knowledge of our historical identity and achievement, to heal the traumatized and disoriented psyche, and to serve as “a means of bringing us closer to our (continental) African brothers and sisters” and of revealing and releasing a capacity for creativity and liberation, which historical and current conditions of oppression tend to hide, hinder and discourage. This film stresses the real return does not mean physical return, but “return culturally, psychologically and spiritually,” recovering views and values that aid in the revolutionary struggle and the recovery of ourselves. The “cultural revolution will be a journey to our recovery of ourselves. In fact, in the liberation struggle, “culture provides the bases for revolution and recovery.” And for me and others like me, this means the recovery of the best of what it means to be African and human, and using it to liberate ourselves and expand the realm of human freedom and flourishing in the world. So, if you can truly see the signs and symbols of the conscious mind, then you should be able to see that this film expresses the indispensability of culture as a weapon and way of liberational struggle and cultural revolution as a process and practice which precedes, aids and sustains the larger liberation struggle and with such sight you should also be able to see that cultural nationalism is inherent in any real and revolutionary nationalism. This film expresses that the defining feature of a nation or people is its culture; that for a people to be and free itself, it must be self-conscious, self-determining, and rooted in its own culture; and that the quality of its life and the success of its liberation depend on its waging cultural revolution within and political revolution without, producing a radical transformation of both self and society.

You maybe can love another person from the bottom of your heart without self-work but in the end the relationship can't survive if you don't accept yourself and If you are not the person you want to be. Every single person in your life is a mirror of your own shadows and will confront you with those. Either the person helps you getting to know your shadows or you have to find them on your own. Both ways are possible. Otherwise those shadows will haunt you so you'll never find piece and true love (for yourself). So in the end this songs presents to me the hard and long path of working on myself, which causes so much pain, tears, resistance but in the end I have to accept myself to let other people into my heart, dont push them away, love them and be one with them! Much love!

As I am writing this today, a few days like maybe 2 3 days ago I can't remember whether this song appeared own my insta feed or I searched for it but after that listening to song I was totally captivated by it. Its not first time I am hearing but never felt it that way. I always Adore Shree Krishna as My Whole Name is from his only and I also try to live up to the Name. I am having govt job exm in the coming days and I was very scared. So I am Chanting Hanuman Chalisa 7 TIMES a day. Guys who prepare for CGL exams know how much hectic it is to prepare for it. So yeah coming back to the song. I used to sing it in my head and a few nights ago I told my mother that I would like to visit Kedarnath one day. And today my mother brought a sacred thread that was given to her by one of her friends in school and she said that it was brought to her  by her husband who went to Kedarnath. For a few minutes I literally cried and not knowing what to do and then I searched for this song and cried again. I always used to had short temper when I was a kid and my grandmother used to say Shiv Shiv by hitting my head. So I am just speechless and I exactly dont know what to say or what I should conclude from this but I just wanted to share with you all. Thanks for hearing me out

I listened to a lot of Tamil songs as a kid, began to shift to Hindi as a teen and finally entered English songs before 11th grade. I began performing English songs in India and abroad. I'm here from Post-Modern Jukebox's 50's Prom cover of this song. One thing I always do when I hear something from P-MJ that I like, I go and check out the original, to see if I'll like THAT, too.   And by "like", I mean that I'll pop it into my 9000+ "Work" rotation (enough 50's, 60's and 70's pop, rock, soul,  funk and New Wave in there, call it about 15 songs an hour, 600 hours, about 25 days and change without hearing the same song twice), so about once a month I'll hear it and go, "Yeah, that's good, the girl is great, the guy's auto-tuned, but hey, kids these days, you know?"   Yet even with such low standards, I'm lucky if I find one or two grunts a month to put in the march with the rest of the Division.    But THIS one? Sure, it's got a good beat.   But the young lady's face at 0:27?   That made me stick around (all the gratuitous bikini shots of her - sorry, I was so over that kind of thing a good 40 years ago). Then at 1:31, the female singer (Halsey?  Help me out here, I'm not hip to this whole temp hire thing the young people have going on these days) provides the closest thing to actual singing (maybe a little too Disney-teen dream with that touch of the dreaded auto-tune here and there), which is getting damn rare these days.   And THEN she mentions Blink 182.   I mean, I'm not even a FAN of Blink 182, but that's ka-ching: it not only goes into the Work rotation, but it's also going into the Talented 10th Regiment, where under random play I'll hear it about once a day. Well, thanks for the bandwidth - back to P-MJ to see if I land another recruit.

Die Lyrics von "Without Me" (Eminem) können tatsächlich auf eine tiefere philosophische Ebene gehoben werden, wenn man sie im Kontext der Frage nach dem Sinn des Lebens und der menschlichen Existenz betrachtet. Hier einige Deutungen: 1. Identität und Bedeutung im Leben Eminem stellt in den Lyrics mehrfach die Frage nach seiner eigenen Bedeutung und dem Einfluss, den er auf andere hat: “Guess who’s back, back again...” “You created a monster, 'cause nobody wants to see Marshall no more...” Philosophisch betrachtet thematisiert er die Rolle des Individuums im größeren sozialen Kontext. Der Sinn des Lebens wird oft mit der Frage verknüpft, wie sehr man die Welt oder andere Menschen beeinflusst. Eminem scheint sich seiner Unverzichtbarkeit bewusst zu sein, ähnlich wie einige Philosophen die Einzigartigkeit jedes Menschen betonen, z. B. Jean-Paul Sartre in seiner Existenzphilosophie: Jeder Mensch gibt seinem Leben durch seine Handlungen und Entscheidungen Bedeutung. 2. Vergänglichkeit und Unersetzbarkeit Ein zentraler Aspekt des Songs ist das Gefühl, dass etwas fehlt, wenn Eminem nicht da ist ("It feels so empty without me"). Dies könnte im philosophischen Sinne auf die Vergänglichkeit des Lebens und die Einzigartigkeit jedes Moments hindeuten. Martin Heidegger beschreibt das menschliche Leben als ein "Sein-zum-Tode", das heißt, wir leben in der ständigen Auseinandersetzung mit unserer Endlichkeit. Die Lyrics erinnern uns daran, dass wir Spuren hinterlassen wollen, um eine gewisse Unsterblichkeit im Gedächtnis anderer zu erlangen. 3. Rebellion gegen Konventionen und der Sinn des Lebens als Widerstand Der Song ist auch eine Art Kampfansage gegen die Gesellschaft und ihre Regeln: “I'm not the first king of controversy, I am the worst thing since Elvis Presley...” Eminem übernimmt hier eine Rolle als Antiheld, der bewusst gegen gesellschaftliche Normen rebelliert. Philosophisch ließe sich das mit Friedrich Nietzsche vergleichen, der die Idee des Übermenschen und die Überwindung traditioneller Werte propagiert. Der Sinn des Lebens wird hier im Widerstand gegen das Gewohnte gefunden – in der Schaffung neuer Werte und Identitäten. 4. Kollektive und individuelle Verantwortung Eminem thematisiert in "Without Me" die Idee, dass die Welt ihn braucht, um weiterzumachen, aber gleichzeitig kritisiert er die Abhängigkeit der Gesellschaft von äußeren Einflüssen. Dies kann an Albert Camus und dessen Philosophie des Absurdismus erinnern: Der Mensch sucht nach Sinn in einer sinnlosen Welt. Camus sieht den Sinn des Lebens im Mut, das Absurde zu akzeptieren und dennoch weiterzuleben, ähnlich wie Eminem seine eigene Rolle annimmt, trotz der Kämpfe, die er durchlebt. 5. Selbstreflexion und die Rolle des Künstlers Ein weiterer wichtiger Aspekt ist Eminems ständige Selbstreflexion über seine Bedeutung als Künstler. Er fragt sich, was er der Welt zu bieten hat und ob sein Dasein eine Berechtigung hat. Diese Fragen sind eng mit dem humanistischen Gedanken verbunden, dass der Sinn des Lebens in der Kreativität, der Selbstausdruck und der Beitrag zur Kultur liegt. Fazit Die Lyrics von "Without Me" können als eine Reflexion über die menschliche Existenz, den Einfluss des Individuums und die Suche nach Bedeutung gelesen werden. Eminem hinterfragt, was es heißt, gebraucht zu werden, und regt damit eine philosophische Debatte über den Sinn des Lebens an: Ist es der Einfluss, den wir auf andere ausüben? Oder ist es die Akzeptanz, dass wir trotz unserer Vergänglichkeit etwas Einzigartiges in die Welt bringen können?

I hate to be that guy who says he hates to be something, but I hate to be that guy that just is a serious know it all, however I must state that Juice is likely not referring to a lucid dream. A lucid dream is when you realize you are dreaming, but instead waking up if you do everything correctly you end up in a very vivid world. You can then do whatever you want. The lyrics implies that he is actually referring to a possible side effect of lucid dreaming: sleep paralysis. This is only an issue with certain techniques, and this can also just happen if you have a bad sleep schedule. Sleep paralysis is when you wake up but your body believes that you are still asleep. You may feel something heavy on your chest, but you can move. You may also have hallucinations like the ones he described. "I still see your shadows in my room" sounds like a hallucination that he could have had in sleep paralysis.

I've read about the debate of whether there's a love triangle in this song, but I believe Gotye and Kimbra are actually singing directly to each other about their shared relationship. When Kimbra sings "You said that you could let it go and I wouldn't catch you hung up on somebody that you used to know," she's cleverly throwing Gotye's own words back at him. She's saying "You claimed you'd move on easily and I wouldn't find you still obsessing over me (someone you used to know)." Her verse isn't introducing a third person - it's giving us her perspective on the same breakup, suggesting he manipulated her and made her feel everything was her fault. This interpretation makes the song so much more powerful as a two-sided breakup story where each person feels wronged in different ways.
